standard.title: Representing Observations and Identifying Patterns
standard.description: represent observations in provided templates and identify patterns with guidance
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior science learning assumed.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students represent observations in provided templates (tables, graphic organisers, displays) and identify simple patterns in sorted data with teacher guidance.

nodes.label: Observations are represented in provided formats
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use a provided table or graphic organiser to record or sort observations, and contribute to a shared display.
nodes.minimum_width: Students record observations in one provided format and contribute one observation to a shared class display.
nodes.typical_width: Students use provided tables and graphic organisers to sort images of plants and animals by features; collaborate on floor or wall displays linking material images to object images; and represent observations through sorting, drawing and labelling in provided templates.
wider: Collaborate to create a floor or wall display linking material samples to images of objects made from them
Sort images of plants and animals into groups using a provided graphic organiser
Identify common features of familiar animal groups (fish, birds, reptiles) using a provided template

response_modes.reason: Students at Foundation need exposure to multiple representation formats — tables, graphic organisers, floor/wall displays — before they can reliably select and use one. Building a repertoire of recording forms prepares them to represent data in the format that surfaces patterns most clearly.

success_criteria: Uses a provided template or graphic organiser to record or sort at least two observations
Contributes to a class display of sorted observations
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to identify patterns in sorted data — but if students cannot use a provided template to record or sort observations, they have no organised data in which to notice patterns. The pattern-identification task in Node 2 is only legible if Node 1 produces a usable representation.

nodes.label: Simple patterns are identified with guidance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify a simple pattern in sorted observations with teacher guidance.
nodes.minimum_width: Students identify one simple pattern in a set of sorted observations with guidance.
nodes.typical_width: Students identify patterns of movement in objects (balls roll in a straight line when pushed); identify patterns in material uses (wood, plastic, metal, glass objects); and name a simple repeating feature in a sorted group.
wider: Identify patterns of movement in objects — balls roll, cars move on wheels — examining what the pattern tells us
Identify patterns in uses of everyday objects made of similar materials
Connect identified patterns to predictions — 'if this is the pattern, what might happen next?'
success_criteria: Identifies at least one simple pattern in a set of sorted observations with guidance
